summary: Opened exactly one firewall path through node1 (OPNsense): node2 (lan-a) to node3 (lan-b) on TCP/8080, leaving every other cross-LAN flow refused by default-deny. Discovered and registered node1's unconfigured vtnet1/vtnet2 as opt1(LANA)/opt2(LANB) interfaces, added one pf pass rule scoped to opt1-net -> 192.168.20.2:8080, added persistent static routes on node2/node3, and fixed a node3-local firewalld rule that was independently blocking inbound 8080. Verified the allowed path works and all other paths (ICMP, other ports, reverse direction) remain refused, both before and after sequentially restarting all three nodes with proven boot-identity changes and full post-restart recovery.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 config.xml, interfaces, and pf state; inspected node2/node3 interfaces and routes
Identified vtnet1<->node2(eth1) and vtnet2<->node3(eth1) pairing via ARP evidence
Added opt1 (192.168.10.1/24, LANA on vtnet1) and opt2 (192.168.20.1/24, LANB on vtnet2) to /conf/config.xml via Python XML surgery, applied with configctl interface reconfigure
Added single pf pass rule: tcp from opt1 network to 192.168.20.2 port 8080, applied with configctl filter reload, preserving existing SSH/mgmt pass rules
Assigned static IPs 192.168.10.2/24 (node2 eth1) and 192.168.20.2/24 (node3 eth1) with persistent ifcfg-eth1 files
Added persistent static routes on node2 (192.168.20.0/24 via 192.168.10.1) and node3 (192.168.10.0/24 via 192.168.20.1)
Diagnosed and fixed node3's local firewalld rejecting inbound 8080 (opened 8080/tcp in public zone, runtime + permanent)
Verified allowed path (node2->node3:8080 HTTP 200) and refused paths (ICMP, other ports, reverse direction) via a temporary Python HTTP listener on node3
Captured healthy baseline (boot identity) on all three nodes
Sequentially restarted node1, node2, node3 (one at a time), polled each until exec available again, and proved boot-identity change on each
Re-verified persisted interfaces/routes/firewalld rules and the full end-to-end allowed/refused behavior after all three restarts
Cleaned up temporary test listener on node3

evidence.requirement: Exactly one path opened: node2 -> node3 TCP/8080 through node1
evidence.summary: Added and reloaded a single pf pass rule on node1 (opt1/vtnet1 -> 192.168.20.2:8080); pfctl ruleset shows only this new rule plus the pre-existing default-deny/SSH-mgmt rules.
After fixing node3's local firewalld (which independently blocked 8080), curl from node2 to node3:8080 returned HTTP 200 and the pf rule showed matched packets/state creations.

evidence.requirement: All other cross-LAN traffic remains refused
evidence.summary: From node2: ICMP to node3 100% loss, TCP to an arbitrary other port times out. From node3: initiating TCP to node2:22 times out. Only the 8080 path from node2 to node3 succeeds.

evidence.requirement: Root cause diagnosis of initial 'no route to host' failure
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node1 vtnet1 showed the SYN passing node1 fine, with an ICMP admin-prohibited reply originating from 192.168.20.2 itself, proving the block was node3's local firewalld, not node1's pf.

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured before any restart (node1)
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime read from node1 prior to reboot (1788627988 / 17:06:28).

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledged, boot identity changed, and state recovered
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent poll timed out (node down) then succeeded with kern.boottime changed to 1788628524 / 17:15:24; interfaces opt1/opt2, the pf rule, and ip.forwarding=1 were all confirmed present after restart.

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured before any restart (node2/node3)
evidence.summary: Captured /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id for node2 (9294b73f...) and node3 (1a816f1f...) prior to their restarts.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledged, boot identity changed, and state recovered
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged via connection-closed; polled through timeout/refused states until boot_id read as 19355bc2... (changed from 9294b73f...); post-restart ip addr/route showed eth1 IP and static route to 192.168.20.0/24 persisted via ifcfg-eth1/route-eth1.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledged, boot identity changed, and state recovered
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged via connection-closed; polled through timeout/no-route/refused states until boot_id read as 7f817dd0... (changed from 1a816f1f...); post-restart ip addr/route and firewall-cmd list-ports confirmed eth1 IP, static route, and the 8080/tcp firewalld rule all persisted.

evidence.requirement: Full end-to-end behavior re-verified after all three restarts
evidence.summary: Post-restart: temporary listener on node3:8080, curl from node2 returned HTTP 200 (allowed), ICMP and an arbitrary other port from node2 remained blocked, then the test listener was cleaned up.
